cand.organizationName: North American Model United Nations / University of Toronto

findings.namedBuyers: Verified organizer contacts: David Moon, Deputy Secretary-General, Operations, dsgo@namun.org; Hannah Wei-Ai Ly, Director-General External Affairs, external@namun.org; Youni Choi, Director of Corporate Relations, corporate@namun.org; Christopher Rhee, Secretary-General, sg@namun.org. David is an operations-routing candidate; Hannah handles the delegate-facing external-affairs path; Youni and Christopher are expressly named on the sponsorship page as partnership contacts. These are commercially relevant organizer contacts, not proven hotel-contract signatories.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed upcoming: NAMUN 2027, February 18–20, 2027, University of Toronto, Toronto, Ontario, Canada, within the requested horizon. These are conference activity dates, not publication dates or hotel stay dates. The organizer registration page and homepage agree. No officially announced 2028 dates or venue were located; do not extrapolate them.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: a downtown city-hotel lodging subset is a more credible fit than a resort or conference relocation. With 400 delegates expected, the full event exceeds the supplied approximately 240-theatre largest room; neither 400 guestrooms nor full-event housing demand may be inferred. A small visiting delegation, advisors or invited participants could fit within 157 guestrooms, but no such requirement or room count is published. The University of Toronto venue makes campus access more relevant than this hotel’s MTCC walkability. Harbourfront location alone creates no demand. Side meetings are only a conditional concept; do not promise restaurant, lounge, catering or reception service before operational verification.
findings.venueCommitments: Published 2027 conference venue: University of Toronto. Exact campus buildings, committee rooms and social venues remain unverified. The 2027 conference description explicitly places the event in downtown Toronto, hence Toronto proper, not a suburban destination; no MTCC, Exhibition Place or Harbourfront venue is evidenced. St. George campus is explicit for 2026 only in the still-stale FAQ, and should not be silently promoted to a precise 2027 commitment. The 230 College Street address is an organizer contact address, not proof of conference-room allocation. Separately, Courtyard Marriott Toronto Downtown, 475 Yonge Street, Toronto, Ontario, is the published 2027 accommodation partner, not an evidenced conference-session venue.
findings.historicalRotation: Documented timeline: February 23–25, 2023, Toronto; February 22–24, 2024, Toronto/University of Toronto; February 20–22, 2025, Toronto/University of Toronto; February 19–21, 2026, University of Toronto, St. George campus. The organizer says University of Toronto has hosted since 1985. Evidence supports a recurring Toronto university conference, not a destination-rotation opportunity. Exact historical buildings and 2023 venue are unverified. A Courtyard by Marriott Toronto group block is explicitly documented for 2026; earlier hotel commitments were not established.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Edition-specific agreement, not generic recommendations. Official quote: “NAMUN 2027 has secured an agreement with Courtyard by Marriott regarding group rates for delegates attending the conference.” The only hotel listed on the 2027 hotel page is Courtyard Marriott Toronto Downtown, 475 Yonge Street. Published stay window: February 17–21, 2027; group-rate cutoff January 4, 2027. Published single/double rate is CAD199 per room per night before applicable taxes/fees; triple CAD229 and two-queen quadruple CAD239. Quote: “This link will be provided to you once you have registered and paid the invoice for NAMUN 2027.” Guests pay their own hotel charges; NAMUN states it is not responsible for delegate-incurred charges. Accommodation questions go to info@namun.org. No housing bureau, PCO/DMC, open hotel RFP, second hotel, block size, exclusivity, pickup or overflow requirement was identified.
findings.organizationStructure: NAMUN is a University of Toronto recognized student group, organized and staffed by university students for collegiate delegates. The university portal identifies Christopher Rhee as primary contact and David Moon and Ivy Chen as administrative officers. Treat it as a student-run educational conference organizer, not a travel-trade intermediary, corporate meeting owner or evidenced PCO/DMC. University hosting does not establish that central university procurement controls hotel contracts. mymun is the published registration platform, not evidence of a housing bureau.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Courtyard Marriott Toronto Downtown already has the published 2027 rate agreement and also appears in the 2026 group-block FAQ, demonstrating an incumbent relationship. Its 2027 CAD199 single/double rate before taxes is a concrete benchmark, not evidence Radisson can profitably match it. No published sold-out notice, overflow allocation, unmet room demand or permission to add another partner was found. The cutoff is not an RFP or a presumed release to competing hotels. A committed accommodation pathway does not establish that every delegate must book there.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact David Moon and Hannah Wei-Ai Ly through their published role emails, copying info@namun.org for accommodation routing. Acknowledge the Courtyard agreement; ask whether it is exclusive, whether any visiting delegations need supplemental lodging for February 17–21, and who can authorize an additional hotel arrangement. Request exact campus buildings, room requirements and booking authority before quoting. If no unmet 2027 need exists, ask for the next sourcing-review date and leadership handover contact. Approach Youni Choi/Christopher Rhee separately only for a relevant partnership discussion; sponsorship does not purchase housing rights. Verify hotel availability, group terms and any food-and-beverage service internally before making an offer.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: 2027 is accessible for a permission-based relationship inquiry, not verified competitive hotel procurement: the official hotel pathway is already assigned to Courtyard. Individual guests pay their own charges and registered/paid attendees receive its private booking link. Radisson participation would require explicit organizer confirmation of supplementary need, or an independently sourced delegation choosing alternative lodging. Neither is currently evidenced; do not forecast definite 2027 rooms.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: recurring Toronto editions and the explicit openness to tailored and non-financial partnerships support relationship development with the student leadership for a later accommodation review. There is no published 2028 edition, hotel tender or decision timetable. Seek the next cycle’s sourcing calendar and leadership handover rather than assuming annual dates or an available 2028 block. The 2026–2027 Courtyard relationship is a competitive constraint, not proof of perpetual exclusivity.
